title: Rome Wasn't Built in One Turn: Replay-Grounded Reward Signals for Long-Horizon Freeciv Agents
title_zh: 罗马不是一回合建成的：面向长程Freeciv智能体的基于重放的奖励信号

paragraphs.en: 构建CivHarness重放系统与LLM裁判CivTelescope，提供密集奖励训练出显著提升的Freeciv游戏智能体。 Training language-model agents to play long-horizon strategy games is hard because deterministic feedback is sparse and often arrives only at the end of a game. In-game scores can offer dense signals, but they do not reliably predict future outcomes: in 8-68% of position pairs across eight strategy games, the higher-scoring position leads to the worse outcome. We term this phenomenon scoreboard traps. In Freeciv, an open-source turn-based empire-building game where several players manage units, cities, and diplomacy over hundreds of turns, we look into better reward signals for gameplay agents. To facilitate this, we build CivHarness, an open system that saves current game states, branches on different decisions, and replays the game to future turns to provide measurable long-horizon feedback from saved positions. We use CivHarness to train CivTelescope, an LLM Judge that predicts which one of two game positions will yield the better outcome. On scoreboard-trap pairs, CivTelescope is 1.3-2.0 times more accurate than off-the-shelf language models, and it generalizes to new game starts, later turns, and unseen rules. We then train a Freeciv gameplay agent with CivTelescope as a dense reward, and call this recipe CivMarshmallow. When used in the middle stage of the game where scoreboard traps are common, CivMarshmallow reaches an average training phase gain of 8.94 points, 77% more than the best baseline, the end-of-game reward. Over the full 120-turn game, CivMarshmallow uses a hybrid reward that starts from the scoreboard or the end-of-game reward and shifts to CivTelescope as the game advances; this hybrid reward scores highest among the rewards we compare.
paragraphs.zh: 构建CivHarness重放系统与LLM裁判CivTelescope，提供密集奖励，训练出显著提升的Freeciv游戏智能体。训练语言模型智能体玩长时程策略游戏很困难，因为确定性反馈稀疏，且往往只在游戏结束时才出现。 游戏内分数可以提供密集信号，但它们并不能可靠地预测未来结果：在八款策略游戏中，8-68%的局面配对里，分数较高的局面反而导致更差的结果。 我们将这一现象称为记分板陷阱。 Freeciv是一款开源的回合制帝国建设游戏，多名玩家在数百个回合中管理单位、城市和外交。我们在这款游戏中研究更适合游戏智能体的奖励信号。 为此，我们构建了CivHarness，一个开放系统，它可以保存当前游戏状态，在不同决策处分支，并将游戏重放到未来的回合，从而从保存的局面中提供可测量的长时程反馈。 我们使用CivHarness训练CivTelescope，一个LLM裁判，用于预测两个游戏局面中哪一个会带来更好的结果。 在记分板陷阱配对上，CivTelescope的准确率是现成语言模型的1.3-2.0倍，并且它能泛化到新的游戏开局、更晚的回合以及未见过的规则。 随后，我们以CivTelescope作为密集奖励训练了一个Freeciv游戏智能体，并将这一配方称为CivMarshmallow。 在记分板陷阱常见的中局阶段使用时，CivMarshmallow平均训练阶段增益达到8.94分，比最佳基线——游戏结束奖励——高出77%。 在完整的120回合游戏中，CivMarshmallow使用混合奖励，以记分板或游戏结束奖励开始，并随游戏推进转向CivTelescope；在我们比较的各类奖励中，这种混合奖励得分最高。
